title: How gambling houses guard against cheating, loaded dice
summary: Matassa explains why houses need no cheating, dice chants and the evolution of crooked dice.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: As in how to stack the deck against someone? Well, no.

Against someone? I mean, how to... This may... You may find this interesting, but it was so that gambling houses had to learn about how people cheat to protect themselves. And the gambling houses didn't cheat. They didn't need to. If you stayed there and gambled, you lost. It was... It's built into the system. You cannot win. Now, that doesn't mean that occasionally some fools don't win for a little while. Right. But you cannot win. The long... In fact, they had these little chants that you say, the guys would scoop up the dice and return them back to you. They had a little chants that they'd take that literally taunted you. You know? And I remember one until today, because it rhymed. And the guy would scoop up the dice and send it back to you and says, if you stay, you got to go. The longer you stay, the further you go.

Yeah. Meaning, I dare you to throw the dice out and put some money on the table, I'm going to beat you. And if you do it twice, I'm going to beat you twice. If you do it ten times, I'll beat you... You know, that kind of thing. And there were names, you know, all the names for the dice came up. Little Joe and Craps and Four and Eight, the Hard Way, meaning you only got two identical numbers. All those kinds of things. A lot of them I don't remember anymore. And also, how cards were marked.

And the evolution of crooked dice. Listen to this. The original crooked dice were what's called loaded dice. And what they were, were tiny little gold pellets put in the paint. You know, they'd dig out to make the numbers, one here, two there. Right. So, they'd be little gold pellets. So, that side tended to lay down, so the thing on the other side would come up. So, loaded dice was the original thing. Well, the gambling houses, if they suspected somebody using loaded dice, all they had to do was pick the dice up and drop them in a glass of water. And they would...
Right. They would come up and...

They would literally turn around. They'd belly up. Right. So, then they started making them that they, one side was very slick and the opposite side had more friction. And they would tend to go along and flip over easier one way than another. Or that they were geometrically imperfect. They weren't perfect cubes. Okay. And things like that. So, I learned all about things like that and how cards were marked and all that. But it was because the gambling houses had to protect themselves from the clientele. Most people think it's the other way around and it isn't. They don't have to cheat you. Believe me. You just stay there and play. They got you. You know. And...
